predecessors.name: South Seas Mandate
predecessors.text: the former Japanese mandate: 'the Marshall, Mariana, and Caroline Islands' with Palau

successors.name: Republic of the Marshall Islands
successors.text: 'On October 21, 1986, the US ended its administration of the Marshall Islands District'

successors.name: Federated States of Micronesia
successors.text: 'Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and the Mariana Islands districts of the TTPI soon followed on November 3, 1986'

successors.name: Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands
successors.text: the Mariana Islands district, 'new constitution partially effective January 1, 1978, and fully effective November 4, 1986'

successors.name: Palau
successors.text: 'the US and Palau agreed to establish the latter's independence on October 1' (1994), after the Security Council ended Palau's trusteeship on 25 May 1994

ledger.x: 1947: the United States takes the former Japanese mandate as a UN strategic trust: 'The TTPI entered UN trusteeship pursuant to Security Council Resolution 21 on July 18, 1947.'
1951: the Interior Department replaces the Navy and the seat moves from Guam to Saipan: 'The United States Navy controlled the TTPI from a headquarters in Guam until 1951.'
1986: the Marshall Islands leave the trust territory: 'On October 21, 1986, the US ended its administration of the Marshall Islands District' (Compact of Free Association effective 21 October 1986).

1986: Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae and Pohnpei leave the trust territory on 3 November 1986: 'Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and the Mariana Islands districts of the TTPI soon followed on November 3, 1986' (COFA effective 3 November 1986 for the Federated States of Micronesia).

1986: the Mariana Islands district leaves on 3 November 1986 to become the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (constitution 'partially effective January 1, 1978, and fully effective November 4, 1986').
ledger.cpn: Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands

ledger.x: 1994: the last trust territory of the United Nations ends with Palau's independence on 1 October 1994.

certainty.note: Island territory: the border is the coast and the district boundaries of the trusteeship; the free-association relations after 1986 are not territory.
